posts.author: carolebouchard.bsky.social
posts.text: Crazy thing is that without Sinner and Alcaraz, Djokovic would still be piling these Grand Slam titles and the Tour would be dominated by a nearly-40 guy. Which is bonkers.

posts.author: carolebouchard.bsky.social
posts.text: Djokovic was never going to win that match. Going to the semifinals after how he finished Wimbledon and fact he didn’t play until the USO is the real performance. Only surprise here is Auger-Aliassime taking a set out of Sinner. That’s where we are indeed: taking a set. 4 GS finals,3 Sinner-Alcaraz.

Down 0-3 in the 3rd set, and thought bubble appeared over every fan in Arthur Ashe.

"Is Jannik Sinner about to lose in the 3rd round at the US Open?"

The answer? Nope.

Sinner does that thing he does, buckling down and taking control to defeat Denis Shapovalov, 5-7, 6-4, 6-3, 6-3.

posts.text:

6-2, 3-6, 3-0.

posts.text:
Jannik Sinner wins 6-1, 6-4, 6-2 against Lorenzo Musetti

tennissweetspot.substack.com/p/alcaraz-un...

posts.author: carolebouchard.bsky.social
posts.text: Jannik Sinner is only the fourth man in  the Open Era to reach all four Grand Slam finals in a season, after Rod Laver, Roger Federer & Novak Djokovic. Youngest (24) to ever do it since Federer (25). Novak and Roger did it three times. I admit I never thought anyone would join that club before eons.

posts.author: carolebouchard.bsky.social
posts.text: Alcaraz broke the Sinner code at the right time and gets back on the throne. Totally expected him to play that well after losing the Wimbledon final against Jannik: he had a point to make. Didn’t expect Sinner’s game to bug a bit here, also thought his serve issues were behind him but nope.

posts.author: carolebouchard.bsky.social
posts.text: Aryna Sabalenka in NYC rebooted Ghostbusters & got over…herself. This US Open title might be a game-changer for Aryna and she may wanna thank Gauff for beating her in Paris, showing her she wasn’t owed a Grand Slam title just because she wanted one. tennissweetspot.substack.com/p/alcaraz-un...

posts.author: carolebouchard.bsky.social
posts.text: 👀 that Sinner - Bublik score. Reading it’s biggest beat down in UsO second week since Djokovic-Cilic semifinals in 2015. Jannik became youngest man to get 24 wins in Grand Slam in a season since Nadal (22) in 2008.Yeah, he’s locked in the Avengers footsteps now… Alcaraz really got some company here.

posts.author: carolebouchard.bsky.social

posts.author: ticktocktennis.bsky.social
posts.text:
Unstoppable Alcaraz?

For the 7th time in his career, Carlos Alcaraz will play for a grand slam singles title after winning a generational battle with a 24-time slam champion.

The 22yo defeats Novak Djokovic, 6-4, 7-6⁴, 6-2, to reach the US Open final without dropping a set.

posts.author: ticktocktennis.bsky.social
posts.text:
King Carlos!

It didn't rise to the lofty standards of this year's Roland-Garros final, but the result was the same.

Carlos Alcaraz is a grand slam champion once again!

The Spaniard downs world #1 Jannik Sinner, 6-2, 3-6, 6-1, 6-4, to lift his 6th slam title at just 22yo!

posts.author: ticktocktennis.bsky.social
posts.text:
A Cut Above

Carlos Alcaraz is proving to be the anti-Samson.

The 2022 US Open champ seems to be gaining strength and focus after his unexpected haircut.

Sometimes knocked for allowing his mind to wander mid-match, Alcaraz stays fully present through a 7-6³, 6-3, 6-4 win over Arthur Rinderknech.

posts.author: ticktocktennis.bsky.social
posts.text:
That Ol' Alcarazzle Dazzle!

To recap week 1 for our top two men's seeds:

1️⃣Jannik Sinner isn't messing around.
2️⃣Carlos Alcaraz isn't messing around.

WOO BOY!!

Alcaraz puts on a clinic on Ashe Stadium, rattling off the final 7 games to defeat Luciano Darderi, 6-4, 6-4, 6-0.

posts.author: ticktocktennis.bsky.social
posts.text:
It's crazy how much the US Open final matters to the overall 2025 picture

If Sinner wins, he will have 3 of the 4 slam titles, coming 1 POINT AWAY from having all 4

2025 Winner: Sinner

But, if Carlos wins, they tie in slam titles but he dominates in Masters titles. (3 to 0)

2025 Winner: Alcaraz

posts.author: ticktocktennis.bsky.social
posts.text:
Utter Domination

Coming into tonight's match, Alexander Bublik had not been broken in 58 service games.

Jannik Sinner broke him in the first game.

And that was just the beginning of an eye-popping beatdown delivered by the world's #1 player, winning 6-1, 6-1, 6-1 in 78 minutes.

posts.author: ticktocktennis.bsky.social
posts.text:
Ship Shape Shapo!

Denis Shapovalov looks AWFULLY good in his first match in Flushing.

The 27th seed sweeps past Winston-Salem champ Marotn Fucsovics, 6-4, 6-4, 6-0.

Shapo is 1 of 3 men who have won multiple hardcourt titles so far this season. (With Carlos Alcaraz & Felix Auger-Aliassime.)

posts.author: ticktocktennis.bsky.social
posts.text:
Sinner Saves It

Down 0-3 in the 3rd set, and thought bubble appeared over every fan in Arthur Ashe.

"Is Jannik Sinner about to lose in the 3rd round at the US Open?"

The answer? Nope.

Sinner does that thing he does, buckling down and taking control to defeat Denis Shapovalov, 5-7, 6-4, 6-3, 6-3.

posts.author: ticktocktennis.bsky.social
posts.text:
Well, folks.

If Jannik Sinner playing grand slam finals isn't your thing, you might wanna tune out from the US Open now.

Because it's starting the look inevitable.

The defending champion breezes past, arguably, one of the toughest outs in his section of the draw in 3 sets.

posts.text: Irrespective of the outcome against Sinner, FAA over this hard-court swing is kind of what tennis always hoped/expected he would become. posts.author: cambi3.bsky.social
posts.text: Alcaraz is so much more dialled in even if the general barometer for this H2H is Sinner's first serve rate. posts.text: FAA has made a match of this, and that alone is beyond expectation against Night Session Sinner. Hope his body can hold up and can maintain this level consistently.
